evidence: src/application/dtos.ts defines toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto, the only DTO mappers. Every use case imports them and none builds DTOs inline.
src/application/cancel-order-use-case.ts calls order.cancel() and reservations.release(order.lines), so it leaves the rules to the domain and uses the StockReservationService abstraction.
src/application/transition-order-use-case.ts calls order.moveTo(target), so state-transition rules stay in the domain Order and are not repeated here.
src/application/place-order-use-case.ts: assertExecuteRule holds the only check that customerId is required, and reservations.reserve(order.lines) goes through the domain service.

src/application/get-order-use-case.ts, cancel-order-use-case.ts and transition-order-use-case.ts repeat the same one-line findById plus NotFoundError guard. This is minor boilerplate, not a duplicated invariant.
src/application/list-stock-levels-use-case.ts and list-orders-by-state-use-case.ts use the same repository-then-map(toXDto) pattern.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module is one cohesive unit: six use-case classes for the order/stock application, plus a shared dtos.ts. Every use case follows the same pattern. Each one injects domain ports through its constructor (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockReservationService, IdGenerator), has a single execute() method, and maps results through the shared mappers. Order-to-DTO mapping lives only in toOrderDto and stock-level mapping only in toStockLevelDto, and no file builds DTOs inline. State-change rules stay on the domain Order (order.cancel(), order.moveTo(target)) and are not re-implemented in the use cases. Stock reservation and release always go through StockReservationService. The only request-validation rule (customerId is required) appears once, in place-order-use-case.ts. Three use cases repeat the same 'find order or throw NotFoundError' guard. It is a one-line lookup, not a business invariant written in more than one place, so it does not count as a cohesion failure. ListStockLevelsUseCase reads products rather than orders, but it is part of the same inventory/ordering application concern and uses the same DTO-mapping approach.
